F=\frac{N}{D}=\frac{x^{2}-y^{2}}{(x+y)(y^{2}+xy-2x^{2})}.

Since \(x^{2}-y^{2}=(x-y)(x+y)\),

\[
F^{-1}= \frac{(x+y)(y^{2}+xy-2x^{2})}{x^{2}-y^{2}}
      =\frac{y^{2}+xy-2x^{2}}{x-y}.
\]

Factor the numerator:

\[
y^{2}+xy-2x^{2}=-(x-y)(2x+y).
\]

Hence  

\[
F^{-1}= -\,(2x+y).
\]

---

### 4.  Add the remaining term  

The original expression equals  

\[
F^{-1}+2\sqrt[6]{a}= -(2x+y)+2x=-y.
\]

Returning to \(x=\sqrt[6]{a},\;y=\sqrt[6]{b}\),

\[
\boxed{-\sqrt[6]{b}}.
\]

(The simplification is valid for \(a,b>0\) and \(a\neq b\) so that no denominator vanishes.)<|eot_id|> <|end_of_text|>
